title: Interdisciplinarity and PROMs (Patient-Reported Outcome Measures) in the Context of Peri- and Postoperative Care for Major Amputations
summary:
Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a condition of the blood vessels in which blood flow to the legs or arms is no longer sufficient. This is caused by deposits (known as plaques) in the arteries, which can narrow the vessels or even block them completely. As a result, less oxygen reaches the muscles and tissues.
When PAD is very advanced, blood flow sometimes cannot be improved, or permanent damage has already occurred. In such cases, amputation is often the only remaining option to eliminate pain caused by oxygen deprivation and to completely remove dead or infected tissue.
After an amputation, the most important goal is to restore mobility, independence, and quality of life as much as possible. In addition to medical and rehabilitative care, this often requires social services support, home care, and, if possible, a barrier-free living environment. Many different professionals are therefore involved in the care process, such as nursing staff, physical therapists, and social services.
As part of this study, joint, structured rounds involving members of various professional groups will take place over three days. The goal is to improve communication between the professional groups and to enhance the quality of care and patient safety. We intend to use the collected data to determine whether the concept of an interdisciplinary rounds improves care for amputee patients.
In addition, we would like to collect additional data after 6 months to analyze the patients’ overall situation over the long term. This includes, on the one hand, information on mobility or the use of a prosthesis, and on the other hand, important data that cannot be directly measured, such as independence and quality of life. We would like to collect this data using so-called PROMs (Patient-Reported Outcome Measures) in questionnaires. The data will be used exclusively for scientific purposes.

interventions.name: Patients scheduled for major amputation receive perioperative and postoperative care through interdisciplinary amputation rounds ("interdisziplinäre Amputationsvisiten") and are surveyed after 6 months using PROMs to assess their functional ability, independence, and quality of life

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent to participate
- Irreversible leg ischemia
- Chronic, irreversible tissue loss in the lower extremities
- Stage III–IV peripheral arterial disease (PAD) according to the Fontaine classification, with no possibility of revascularization
Exclusion criteria:
- Language barriers
- Other communication difficulties, such as aphasia following a stroke
